cues: Wish and if only behave like a type two or type three if clause: the tense goes one step back to show the thing is not so.
I wish I knew the answer: I don't.
I wish I had listened to you: I didn't.
I wish you would stop shouting: annoyance.
If only I had known earlier.
It is high time we left: something overdue, with the past.
And he talks as if he knew everything.
So never I wish I would have gone, but I wish I had gone; and it is time we went, not go.
